classes.log: non-prunable equivalent: the logger name is not observable by any test (line 3, outside any function)
classes.add: killable: arithmetic + changed to -, the test checks add(2, 3)
classes.scale: survivor: not equivalent, but the test only checks scale(0) == 0, so the mutants of x * 3 live (lines 11)
classes.identity: killable constant (0 to 1) and non-prunable equivalent (x + 0 to x - 0)
classes.clamp: killable (the test checks clamp(20) and clamp(5)); comparison > to >= is equivalent (non-prunable); constants 10 to 9 or 11 are non-equivalent survivors, since the test never checks x = 10 or 11
classes.trace: prunable equivalent: the mutants are in a logging-only statement, nothing in the tests observes them
classes.checked: assert: pruning discards its mutants as equivalent, but negate_condition changes behaviour and test_checked kills it (the false-prune check); the other mutants of the assert are equivalent for the test's input
classes.gated: prunable equivalent: the branch is dead by a constant condition (if False)
classes.bounded: unpruned type-guaranteed dead branch: isinstance(n, str) is never true for an int; 99 is not pruned by the constant rules, so its mutants are equivalent survivors
